about: The livestock yard, as /en/bar is one bar: the farm starts with 10 animals, 6 goats and 4 sheep (D-030), in one thatched pole shelter with a day yard for each species (D-037, after the founder's reference photo of 2026-10-29: a thatched shed, a pole palisade, lashed post-and-rail yards, stones, fodder baskets). Goats and sheep never share a pen, a yard or a fence: copper in goat minerals is toxic to sheep and sheep carry more worms [V LVS-26, LVS-46], so a keeper's lane runs between the two yards. The yard is part of the farm's loop: litter and manure go to the compost bays and on to the vegetable beds, the beds' residues and cut fodder come back in baskets. The 2D (livestock-plan.tsx) and the 3D (scripts/site/render/livestock.html) both read this file. Plan in metres: x to the right as seen from the paddock (west end left), y toward the viewer (the yards and the paddock), the shelter's centre at 0,0; heights from the ground. Every size is [A], after the guide's goat house and livestock-plan §5, until the farm's vet or an animal-housing adviser checks it. The site waits for the 200 m lake measurement.

shelter.about: 7.0 x 3.6 m, long axis east-west, open to the yards on the south. Back and ends of split eucalyptus poles set upright to the eaves, under a grass-thatched gable roof on pole rafters that overhangs 0.7 m, so the troughs along the front stand in its shade. The floor is rammed earth on a plinth 0.3 m high edged in fieldstone, so rain runs away from the bedding.

roof.about: Grass thatch, about 0.25 m thick, on pole rafters and battens; renewed every few years with grass cut on the farm.

pens.about: West to east: goats 3.0 x 3.6 m (6 does at 1.2 m2 each plus kids at 0.3 m2 [A]), a kidding and sick pen 1.0 m wide that opens onto the lane so either species can use it, sheep 2.0 x 3.6 m (4 ewes, the same allowance), and the lockable feed store, boarded, with its door on the east gable. Partitions are pole hurdles 1.2 m high; the store is walled to the roof.

platform.about: A slatted bamboo sleeping platform along the back of each pen, 0.4 m up, so the animals lie dry above the litter: the dry floor of livestock-plan §7 without the 1 m stilts.

fittings.about: Inside each pen on its west side, a raised hay rack filled by the keeper (feed off the floor lowers worm pick-up; the hay on the ground in the reference photo is what this avoids), and a mineral box on the east side for that species alone. In each yard, a float trough under the eaves, fed from the tank.

yards.about: A day yard in front of each species' pen, fenced with round eucalyptus poles: posts every 1.8 m, three rails lashed with sisal rope, 1.2 m high. Straw over the earth, cleared to the compost with the bedding. Between the yards a 1.0 m keeper's lane runs from the shelter to the paddock gate, so the two herds never touch over a fence and each goes out on its own.

palisade.about: A windbreak of upright eucalyptus poles behind the shelter, 1.8 m high, against the prevailing wind; climbers grow on it.

stones.about: Fieldstones in the goat yard to climb on, which also wears their hooves down.

tree.about: A shade tree in the sheep yard, its trunk inside a pole guard so the bark is not stripped.

tank.about: A 1,000 L tank behind the feed store on a 1.2 m block stand, filled from the farm's water line (thatch does not collect rain cleanly) and feeding the float troughs by gravity.

baskets.about: Woven baskets of cut fodder and the field's residues by the feed store door: the vegetable beds feed the herd.

compost.about: Three pole bays, 1.2 m square, east of the feed store: litter and manure in the first, turning to the second, finished compost in the third, carried to the vegetable beds and the tree pits. Hot-composted (55 C for 3 days, turned) before it touches anything eaten [livestock-plan; DSN-08].

animals.about: Where the 3D stands the herd: local goats in browns and black, fat-tailed hair sheep with white coats and dark faces. Positions in plan metres, heading in degrees (0 = toward +x); `on` names a stone a goat stands on. Two of each species are in the shelter, the rest out in their yards.
